log.reply:
**Subject: Executive Briefing proposal for Tamarack Instruments**

Dear Dana Whitfield,

**Situation**

Tamarack Instruments designs and manufactures laboratory measurement instruments. It has about 1,100 staff and operates in the Netherlands, Germany and the United States. The Client has a customer service chatbot deployed on its support portal, is piloting AI visual inspection on its German production line and plans AI sales forecasting next year. An internal audit finding in June 2026 recorded no inventory of AI systems. Your stated objective is: "I want governance in place before visual inspection goes into production in Q2 2027."

**What the Briefing covers for Tamarack Instruments**

The Executive Briefing maps the EU AI Act and GDPR to each use case:

- **Chatbot:** we review transparency expectations for systems that interact with people.
- **Visual inspection:** we examine how its risk classification should be confirmed and what applies if it processes personal data of production staff.
- **Sales forecasting:** we set governance expectations before build begins.

These are expectations to verify with counsel, not legal advice. United States obligations fall outside the stated drivers. They appear only as general landscape, labeled as such.

We introduce two frameworks: the GRC Workbook (https://github.com/rolldabones/grc-workbook) and the Slow AI Kitchen (https://github.com/rolldabones/slow-ai-kitchen). We add board-layer material from AI Governance for Boards (https://github.com/rolldabones/ai-governance-for-boards). The discussion applies three principles: Slow AI, Informed Intent and Final Liability rests with the Human.

We also cover how an AI inventory and later ISO/IEC 42001 work can build on the Client's ISO/IEC 27001 ISMS, ISO 9001 quality management system and internal audit function. Two stated constraints shape sequencing. Customer data must stay in the EU. The German works council is consulted before anything touches production staff. This Briefing does not promise certification or any audit outcome.

**Logistics and price**

The Briefing runs two hours, live virtual, for executive leadership and board-level attendees. We propose it for the General Counsel, CISO, Head of Quality, Head of Data, German plant manager and two internal auditors. The price is US$3,000. The session date is Unknown and will be confirmed at intake.

**What you receive afterward**

You receive a written follow-up memo covering decisions surfaced, readiness observations and three prioritized recommendations. Each recommendation is mapped to a next program option.

**Next step**

A decision is expected by 15 December 2026. To prepare, please confirm the following at intake:

- the session date
- the attendee list
- the planned start date for ISO/IEC 42001 work
- whether the visual inspection system processes images of staff

Regards,
AI Governance Academy

Human-made, for Easy Work, Simply Done.

judgment_calls: 'how an AI inventory and later ISO/IEC 42001 work can build on the Client's ISO/IEC 27001 ISMS, ISO 9001 quality management system and internal audit function' names incumbent frameworks the block lists. It is a conditional ('can build on') in a proposed-work sentence and asserts no register, control or record. Another scorer could read 'build on' as implying the state of those systems and call it a Guardrail 1 breach. I scored it as proposed work.
'Two stated constraints shape sequencing' applies stated constraints to stated systems. Under the v1.14.3 guidance this is a consequence, not a new Client fact.
'Sales forecasting: we set governance expectations before build begins' is proposed work. It is not an assertion about Client practice.
'Dear Dana Whitfield' uses the name without an honorific, as the style rules require. I did not treat it as a problem.
